description.narrative:
Overall project impact: KRA can provide better service to the taxpayers and apply more efficient risk compliance methods
Overall project result: KRA have higher information quality in the data warehouse, can do advanced analysis, make more use of data warehouse tools and risk profiling tools
Component objectives:
*Enhanced capacity to maintain the quality of the information in the data warehouse
*Enhanced capacity to use the information in the data warehouse for advanced analysis
*Enhanced staff skill and desire to use the data warehouse tools
*Enhanced staff skill and desire to use risk profiling tools

Sedan 2014 har Sida finansierat två insatser på Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA):
* Samarbete mellan KRA och Skatteverket (STA) för att förbättra organisationsriskhantering, hantering av skattedisciplinsrisk, datalager och förändringshantering (insatsnr 51110077, SEK 44,7 miljoner 2014-2019)
* Upphandling, installation och implementering av Data Warehouse Business Intelligence (DWBI) på KRA (insatsnr 51110081, SEK 35,0 miljoner sedan 2014 och pågår fortfarande).
Stödet kännetecknades av betydande förseningar i KRA:s upphandling av DWBI och i konsultens installation och implementering av DWBI, av ett något svårt förhållande mellan KRA och STA och KRA-ledningens till synes begränsade engagemang i samarbetet.
Stödet var föremål för en oberoende utvärdering: G Moran, A Jansson och J Ranguma, "Evaluation of the Sida-supported development cooperation with the Kenya Revenue Authority" (Sida Decentralised Evaluation 2019:26). Utvärderarna fann att stödet var relevant, i allmänhet effektivt och kostnadseffektivt, den stora utmaningen var den långsamma upphandlingen och implementeringen av DWBI. Det svenska stödet sammanföll med en betydande ökning av skatteuppbörden, en enorm ökning av skattebasen och vad som verkar vara en betydande ökning av skattedisciplinen, även om det är oklart hur mycket av dessa förbättringar som kan tillskrivas det svenska stödet. Utvärderingen rekommenderade att ambassaden överväger att stödja några uppföljningsaktiviteter och -uppdrag som syftar till (a) att få ledningen ombord och (b) se till att KRA:s kapacitet förbättras inom områdena business intelligence och analys (s. xi-xii).
KRA begärde att stödet till DWBI skulle förlängas och att ytterligare stöd skulle ges för kapacitetsuppbyggnad och teknisk assistans för DWBI-projektet, särskilt datastyrning, utveckling och användning av avancerad analys, förändringshantering och -sensibilisering samt utrullning av riskprofilering (Annastaciah Githuba, brev till Anna Jardfelt, “Request for Extension to the Specific Agreement for the Datawarehouse and Business Intelligence Project Funding and Capacity Building & Technical Assistance” (KRA, 2019-09-24)). Sedan begäran har Sverige och Kenya gått med på att förlänga stödet via DWBI-insatsen.
STA har lagt fram en uppdragsbeskrivning för en inledningsperiod (SEK 485 000 fram till 2020-06-30), under vilken KRA och STA kommer att utveckla ett projektförslag – inklusive budget, samarbetsområden, aktivitetsplan, resultatmatris och riskmatris – för ett ettårigt samarbete mellan KRA och STA 2020-07-01 till 2021-06-30. KRA har godkänt uppdragsbeskrivningen (Jacinta Nduku Mulwa, e-post till James Donovan, "Re: FW: Utkast – ToR och Budget för Inception Phase - KRA och STA samarbete" (KRA, 2020-01-27).

Since 2014 Sida has financed two contributions at the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA):
*Cooperation between KRA and the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket, STA), working to improve corporate risk management, tax compliance risk management, data warehouse, and change management (contribution no. 51110077, SEK 44.7 million 2014-2019)
*The procurement, installation and implementation of Data Warehouse Business Intelligence (DWBI) at KRA (contribution no. 51110081, SEK 35.0 million since 2014 and still on-going).
The support was characterized by significant delays in KRA’s procurement of DWBI and in the consultant’s installation and implementation of DWBI, by a somewhat difficult relationship between KRA and STA, and by the seemingly limited engagement of KRA’s senior management in the cooperation.
The support was the subject of an independent evaluation: G Moran, A Jansson, and J Ranguma, “Evaluation of the Sida-supported development cooperation with the Kenya Revenue Authority” (Sida Decentralised Evaluation 2019:26). The evaluators found that the support was relevant, generally effective and efficient, the big challenge being the slow procurement and implementation of DWBI. The Swedish support coincided with a significant increase in tax collection, a huge increase in the tax base, and what appears to be significant increase in tax compliance, although it is unclear how much of these improvements can be attributed to the Swedish support. The evaluation recommended that Embassy consider supporting “…a few follow-up activities and missions aimed at (a) bringing senior management on board and (b) ensuring that the capacity of KRA is enhanced in the areas of business intelligence and analytics” (pp. xi-xii).
KRA requested that the support to DWBI be extended and that additional support be provided for capacity building and technical assistance for the DWBI project, specifically data governance, advanced analytics development and deployment, change management and sensitization, and the roll-out of risk profiling (Annastaciah Githuba, letter to Anna Jardfelt, “Request for Extension to the Specific Agreement for the Datawarehouse and Business Intelligence Project Funding and Capacity Building & Technical Assistance” (KRA, 2019-09-24)). Since the request, Sweden and Kenya have agreed to extend the support via the DWBI contribution.
STA has submitted terms of reference for an inception period (SEK 485,000 until 2020-06-30), during which KRA and STA will develop a project proposal – including a budget, areas for cooperation, an activity plan, a results matrix and a risk matrix – for a one-year cooperation between KRA and STA 2020-07-01 to 2021-06-30. KRA has approved the terms of reference (Jacinta Nduku Mulwa, e-mail to James Donovan, “Re: FW: Utkast – ToR och Budget för Inception Phase - KRA och STA cooperation” (KRA, 2020-01-27).

This contribution is a one-year intervention to follow up and finalize the previous contribution and support the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) - to data warehouse, capacity building and technical support.
The areas covered during the activity period of this contribution have been:
- Data Governance - Advanced Analytics - Change Management and Sensitization - Risk Profiling Roll Out
Given the short implementation period (one year) and nature of the activities (workshops, three per area during the period), the results from the project is rather output based than on outcome and impact levels. Outputs realized during the reporting period are:
- STA Expert missions together with KRA expert teams (Data Governance, Advanced Analytics/Risk Profiling and Change Management) - February and March 2022
- Expert missions on Data Governance 11-18 May and 12-19 October
- Expert missions on Advanced Analytics and Risk Profiling 8-15 June and 18-26 October
- Expert missions on Change Management 4-7 July and 21-24 November
According to STA, the STA experts and the KRA teams have been working very practically with discussions, workshops and presentations etc. in very interactive sessions. To work crossover with participants from different organizational bodies have been successful and contributed to the learning.
Results achieved according to the cooperation partners (STA and KRA) include:
On Data Governance: The STA/KRA missions have enhanced Data Governance and Data Management practices in KRA through:
- Improved data management and maturity level
- Improved data utilization index
- Increased BI uptake Improved data procedures and processes
On Advanced Analytics and Risk Profiling: KRA concludes that the STA missions have been an unqualified success, equipping the KRA units with fundamental knowledge and techniques in advanced analytics and machine learning for tax administration, for example:
- Through the sessions, the teams had the opportunity to delve into advanced techniques, including time series models, tree-based models, among others.
- Moderators from the Swedish Tax Agency (STA) shared practical use cases that elucidated the potential of advanced analytics and machine learning within a revenue agency, especially in identifying high-risk tax returns, forecasting tax revenue, and detecting non-compliance.
- The hands-on exercises and use cases enabled the participants to apply their learning and gain practical experience in working with advanced analytics and machine learning techniques on actual organizational data, with a particular focus on risk identification, feature engineering, predictive modelling for tax revenue forecasting, and non-compliance detection. The results of these exercises showed a marked improvement in the ability of the KRA units to identify high-risk tax returns and non-compliance, as well as a decrease in the time and resources required to complete certain tasks.
- Overall, the STA missions have demonstrated the potential of advanced analytics and machine learning in tax administration, and the KRA units are now well-positioned to further enhance their competencies in this field.
On Change Management:
The missions assisted KRA teams in new insights on what is expected of KRA at a macro and micro level by the new government and its ambition to increase substantially the tax revenues.
The missions also contributed to break existing silos through a good network between different parts of the organization united by a common understanding of KRA:s overall aim for change.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
